title: Sausage and Peppers
subtitle: Italian sausages with bell peppers and onions in tomato
excerpt: Sausage and peppers is an Italian-American street food and home kitchen staple: pork sausages cooked in a pan with peppers, onion, garlic, and a little tomato until everything is soft and the sausages are cooked through. Goes in a roll or on a plate.
sourceNotes: Sausage and peppers is an Italian-American dish widely associated with street festivals in New York and New Jersey. It's a simple one-pan preparation with southern Italian origins.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made ahead and reheated gently. The peppers soften further but it's still good.

content.text: Sausage and peppers is a one-pan dish: pork sausages browned in a frying pan, then cooked down with sliced onions, peppers, garlic, and a little tomato sauce until everything is soft and the sausages are properly cooked through. Serve in a bread roll at a street fair, or on a plate with polenta or pasta at home.

items.prepNote: pork, ideally Italian-style or fennel sausages

content.text: Heat {{olive-oil}} in a large, wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add {{sausages-pork}} and cook, turning occasionally, for five to six minutes until browned all over. They won't be cooked through yet. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan, add {{onion}} and cook for five minutes until beginning to soften. Add {{pepper-red}}, {{pepper-green}}, and {{garlic}}. Cook for another five minutes, stirring, until the peppers are soft and slightly charred at the edges.
Add {{oregano-dried}}, {{chilli-flakes}} if using, and {{tinned-tomatoes}}. Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Return the sausages to the pan, nestling them among the peppers. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover partially, and cook for 15 minutes, turning the sausages halfway through, until they are cooked through and the sauce has thickened.

items.cause: Heat too high, or sausages pricked before cooking.
items.fix: Keep the heat at medium: a steady sizzle without violent spitting. Don't prick pork sausages before frying.

items.symptom: The peppers are pale and soft, not slightly charred
items.cause: Too much liquid in the pan, or heat too low.
items.fix: Fry the peppers on a higher heat and don't add any liquid until after they're softened and beginning to colour.

items.symptom: The sauce is too dry and sticking to the pan
items.cause: Tomatoes too dry, or sauce reduced too much.
items.fix: Add a splash of water (50 ml) to the pan and stir. The sauce should be loose enough to coat the vegetables without being watery.

items.symptom: The sausages are pink in the middle
items.cause: Not cooked long enough in the final stage.
items.fix: Check by cutting one open: the inside should be uniformly beige with no pink. Continue cooking for another five minutes.

content.text: Sausage and peppers is the smell of the Italian-American street festival: the vast griddle pans on gas burners, the long queues for bread rolls, the peppers and onions caramelising alongside the sausages. At home it's a weeknight staple, made in one pan with very little effort. The dish works best with Italian-style pork sausages with fennel or chilli, but any good-quality pork sausage will do.
